profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review between the lead ML researcher and the evaluation/infrastructure researcher for a workshop submission that extends a prior CREMA-D multimodal emotion-recognition study. The current proposal keeps CNN feature extractors for audio and video, compares GRU, LSTM, Transformer, and temporal max pooling as sequence modules, and adds a stronger reproducibility section plus a revised evaluation table. The agenda is to decide whether the design is ready for the final experiment pass and paper freeze: they will review whether the comparison setup is considered 'locked', whether the evaluation package is 'complete', whether the planned ablation on temporal context is already covered by the existing pipeline, and whether the rerun can proceed on the 'standard CREMA-D split' without further design changes. The expected outcome is a verbal approval to proceed with one final run and drafting updates, while both participants leave believing they agreed on the same execution details.

members.name: Dr. Selin Aras
members.expertise: Multimodal representation learning, affective computing, sequence-model benchmarking
members.background: Selin leads a small academic-industry collaboration on multimodal emotion recognition and wrote the current design proposal by adapting an earlier internal benchmark on CREMA-D into a workshop paper format.
members.private_state: She wants the design review to end with approval today so the team can finish runs before the workshop deadline; she is especially concerned about avoiding any late changes that would force retraining all models.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says the comparison is 'locked', it means architecture and data preprocessing are frozen, but they can still change aggregation and reporting choices at analysis time without reopening design review.
The 'standard CREMA-D split' refers to the speaker-independent 70/15/15 split used in her group's recent internal benchmark, not necessarily the exact split from older papers.

A 'complete' evaluation package for a design review means macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1 over the six emotion classes plus a confusion matrix in the appendix; per-actor or repeated-seed breakdowns are optional polish.

The planned temporal-context ablation is already satisfied if each model sees the same fixed 16-frame visual window and aligned audio chunk, because context length is a preprocessing constant rather than part of the model design.

members.name: Emre Tunc
members.role: Research Engineer for Evaluation and Reproducibility
members.expertise: Experimental pipelines, benchmark replication, statistical reporting for ML systems
members.background: Emre maintains the lab's experiment runner and was asked to harden the proposal into a reproducible benchmark package suitable for release after submission.
members.private_state: He wants the review to preserve replicability and avoid reviewer criticism about instability or hidden protocol choices, but he does not want to sound obstructive if Selin is aiming for quick sign-off.
hidden_assumptions: When a comparison is 'locked', all details that affect the final table are frozen, including averaging convention, number of seeds, and checkpoint-selection rule, because otherwise the benchmark is not truly locked.

The 'standard CREMA-D split' means the actor-held-out split protocol used in the original replication notes he inherited, where a fixed subset of speakers is reserved rather than a random 70/15/15 partition.

A 'complete' evaluation package includes mean and standard deviation over at least three seeds, plus per-class metrics, because a single aggregate table is not enough for a claim that models perform similarly.

The temporal-context ablation only counts as covered if context length is explicitly varied as an experimental factor (for example 8, 16, and 32 frames); a fixed 16-frame pipeline does not constitute an ablation.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the comparison being 'locked'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the comparison setup is 'locked' before the final rerun.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means model architectures, feature extraction, and train/validation/test data flow are fixed; reporting-level choices like aggregation format or checkpoint summarization can still be finalized afterward.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means every element that can affect the final benchmark table is fixed now, including averaging convention, seed count, and checkpoint-selection rule.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In research meetings, 'locked' is a familiar shorthand that usually signals general readiness, so each assumes the other shares the same practical boundary without needing to enumerate everything.

misalignment_points.topic: Which 'standard CREMA-D split' they are approving
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to run on the 'standard CREMA-D split'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is referring to the lab's current speaker-independent 70/15/15 split artifact used in the latest internal benchmark folder.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is referring to the actor-held-out split protocol from older replication notes and a different fixed speaker partition.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are talking about the same dataset and both protocols are plausible, established, and internally documented as 'standard', so the phrase feels precise enough even though it points to different concrete split files.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They discuss whether the evaluation section is 'complete enough for the paper'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes completeness means the main aggregate metrics table and a confusion matrix are sufficient for design approval; extra breakdowns can be added only if time permits.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes completeness requires multi-seed statistics and per-class breakdowns before the paper can legitimately claim close performance among models.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both endorse rigor and both mention the same high-level metrics, so their standards differ silently in threshold rather than in explicit objective.

misalignment_points.topic: Whether the temporal-context ablation is already covered
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the current plan 'already covers the context ablation'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 treats context ablation as in scope if all models consume the same predefined 16-frame/aligned-audio window, since this controls temporal context consistently across architectures.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 treats context ablation as in scope only if the proposal includes separate runs that vary the context window length itself.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because they are reviewing a design rather than inventing experiments from scratch, the phrase 'covers the ablation' sounds like confirming existing intent, and neither expects the other to reinterpret the boundary of what counts as an ablation.

Reporting details can still be tidied afterward without touching the actual experiment design.
